reasoning_summary: Selected features prioritize stable, interpretable credit risk signals with zero missingness and broad semantic coverage. External scores (EXT_SOURCE) lead due to their strong predictive power and stability. Core demographic and employment features (age, employment days, occupation, income type, education, gender, family and housing status) are included for interpretability and durability. Bureau credit and debt aggregates are chosen focusing on mean and max aggregates to avoid redundancy and ensure stable signals of indebtedness, credit history, and leverage. Installment repayment behavior features are selected emphasizing mean and key behavioral metrics (payment ratio, lateness, underpayment) for durable repayment signals. Delinquency and POS cash balance features are included for customer payment behavior insights. Previous application features are included with focus on amount, timing, and decision-related aggregates, avoiding excessive redundancy by selecting representative statistics. Credit card utilization features are excluded due to lower variance and potential instability. Building and living area features are excluded due to lower direct credit risk interpretability and potential redundancy. Overall, the selection balances stability, coverage, interpretability, and redundancy control to provide a robust candidate pool for downstream modeling.
selection_principles: stability: prefer features with zero missingness and known durable credit-risk meaning
coverage: ensure broad semantic groups are represented (external scores, demographics, bureau, repayment behavior, delinquency, previous applications)
redundancy control: select representative aggregates (mean, max) within semantic groups, avoid near-duplicate or low-variance features
interpretability: favor features understandable and defensible in credit risk scorecard reviews
avoid leakage: exclude features that may reflect policy or process artifacts or sparse tail variables
